about: The links between host memory and a GPU, one row per kind, in the order they are tried (target/host_links.py). detect: the detector names, tried in order; the first that answers decides the kind. rate: how the link's own rate is read when no copy was measured (the measured copy rate, target/host.h2d, always comes first): line_code (GT/s x lanes x the line code's payload bits per code bits / 8, a row [up to GT/s, payload, code]:  a wire rate: an upper bound), reported (the tool's stated link speed), memory_bandwidth (no link: the GPU reads system memory at the memory's own bandwidth), none (not known). semantics: how an engine BoltBeam sets up uses the link (copy: experts copied to GPU memory before use; direct_read: read in place over the link during the GEMM; none: no copy, plain memory reads); can: what the hardware allows. verified_by: the detectors whose answer has been checked on real hardware (verified_on says where); a record is verified only when one of them decided it and every fact in requires is known and holds (requires_why says what is missing otherwise), else the output says "not verified on this hardware". The fallback row is the record when no detector answers.

links.verified_on: vendor_shares_memory: Apple M-series, Mac mini (boltbeam doctor's host rows and host.facts with no bus id, 2026-11-11)
links.unverified_cases: runtime_integrated answering yes (a DGX Spark-class GB10 through CUDA, an MI300A- or Strix Halo-class APU through HIP): never run on such a chip; the record is unverified and says so

words.name: shared memory
words.detail: none: the GPU is part of the chip and shares the CPU's memory, so there is no link to read
words.reads: reads from shared memory at the memory's {gbs} GB/s

sources: target/vendors.py: a vendor row with profile None shares the CPU's memory (Apple)
cuda.h (CUDA 13.2): CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_INTEGRATED = 18, 'Device is integrated with host memory'

words.name: NVLink-C2C link
words.reads: reads over the NVLink-C2C link at {gbs} GB/s

sources: nvidia-smi manual (docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvidia-smi): -q 'Addressing Mode' is ATS, HMM or None (Linux only); 'nvidia-smi c2c -s' prints the C2C links' status and, when active, their bandwidth; 'GPU C2C Mode' in -q since v530

DGX Station development guide, Mixed Coherency Environment (docs.nvidia.com/dgx/dgx-station-development-guide/coherency.html): nvmlDeviceGetAddressingMode gives ATS for the GB300 (the hardware path on NVLink-C2C systems, the GPU uses the host page tables and reads CPU memory directly) and HMM for a PCIe-attached RTX PRO 6000
nvml.h: NVML_FI_DEV_C2C_LINK_COUNT, NVML_FI_DEV_C2C_LINK_GET_STATUS, NVML_FI_DEV_C2C_LINK_GET_MAX_BW (MB/s, active links)
links.unverified: the exact text of 'nvidia-smi -q' and 'nvidia-smi c2c -s' on a Grace machine (the fixtures follow the manual's field names); whether c2c -s states one direction or both; whether a DGX Spark-class chip (also ATS) should be the unified row instead; an integrated GPU that also reports ATS (DGX Spark class) is caught first by the shared-memory row only when the runtime's integrated answer is saved (boltbeam host)

words.name: PCIe link
words.detail: gen {gen} x{width}: {gbs} GB/s on the wire
words.reads: reads over the PCIe link at {gbs} GB/s

sources: Linux ABI sysfs-bus-pci: max_link_speed, max_link_width, current_link_speed, current_link_width
PCI Express base spec: 8b/10b to 5 GT/s, 128b/130b to 32 GT/s, 242/256 FLIT at 64 GT/s
links.verified_on: RTX 5090 at 0000:06:00.0 (2026-11-11): sysfs 32 GT/s card in a 16 GT/s x16 slot, nvidia-smi pcie.link.gen.max 4 / width.max 16, the CUDA integrated attribute 0
links.requires_why: whether the GPU shares the CPU's memory was not read; boltbeam host asks the GPU runtime
